Text measured by CSS for signs, labels and particles

Type in the field at the bottom of the picture. It's a real <input> drawn by the canvas. Each character you type grows into place and a copy flies up to the sign, and each character you delete breaks into pieces. The canvas knows where each character is from input.createValueRange(). The sign, the book spines and the ticker are elements sized by text-fit and text-box-trim, drawn at the size CSS gave them.

How it works

  • The picture is one 2D canvas. Every label and the input are drawn with drawElementImage() at their offsetWidth and offsetHeight.
  • The sign is 250 px wide in CSS. text-fit: grow scales whatever you type to that width, and text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic makes its box end at the top of the capitals and at the baseline. "Show boxes" outlines each element's box. Turn "Trim" off to see the box that the same text has without it.
  • The book spines use writing-mode: sideways-lr. Each is 132 px along the spine, and text-fit picks the font size, so a short title is drawn large and its book is thick.
  • After each frame in which the field changed, the field's part of the canvas is copied to a second canvas and one rectangle per character is read. A deleted character is cut from that copy as 4 px pieces. A new character is drawn again from the copy: its dark pixels become a coloured, see-through picture of the letter, which is drawn large over the field and once more on a path to the sign.
  • The effects draw over the field. The field itself is drawn where the canvas says it is, so a tap focuses it and the caret and selection are the browser's.

Findings

From Chromium 157 with software rendering. The rows above say what your browser does.

  • Works: text-fit in the picture. The fitted size is what is drawn, and it follows edits and a CSS animation of font-weight with no script. The element's height follows the fitted size, so a short text makes a tall label. This page caps the sign's drawn height at 96 px by scaling the draw.
  • Works: text-box-trim makes the box the ink. With cap alphabetic the first row of the element's picture has ink in it. Descenders and accents fall outside the box and are cut off by the element's picture, which is the stated behaviour of the property and matters for a texture.
  • Works: writing-mode: sideways-lr with text-fit. The fitted axis is the vertical one.
  • Works: createValueRange() rectangles of a drawn input. One call per character. The check compares them with measureText() and reports the difference.
  • Limit: the pieces are pictures. A character in flight is a copy of pixels. The text that can be selected and edited is the field's. This differs from /particles/, where the hit box follows the letters.
  • Not verified here: the on-screen keyboard on a phone (whether the field stays in view when the keyboard opens, and input from predictive text, which can replace a whole word in one event), and whether createValueRange() exists in Chrome 159 on Android. The status line under the picture says which method is in use.
